SDK: inject host-bound runtime into ImportExportContext

ImportExportContext lacks the host-bound ExtensionCommandSdk already available to CommandHandlerContext, forcing importer/exporter packages such as pm-todos to spawn the pm binary for core actions. Duplicate check 2026-07-26: searched all statuses for ImportExportContext, host-bound SDK, importer/exporter execution, and pm-todos spawning; pm-7qjk and pm-1p2u cover registration/test invocation, pm-xzhz covers the runtime, and pm-13bn covers migration, but none inject the runtime into importer/exporter handlers.

ImportExportContext exposes the same host-bound SDK contract needed for in-process core actions; importer/exporter test helpers can inject and exercise it; parity tests prevent CommandHandlerContext and ImportExportContext runtime capability drift; pm-todos can migrate away from spawning pm without private imports; SDK and extension docs describe the lifecycle and compatibility contract
Every extension execution surface receives composable in-process PM primitives from the public SDK
Package authors can build portable import/export integrations without subprocess coupling
GitHub issue #749 reports a real downstream pm-todos blocker after the SDK-first baseline landed
Importer/exporter handlers receive a typed host-bound SDK and can execute supported PM actions in process.
Command handlers receive sdk, but ImportExportContext does not, so importer/exporter handlers must spawn pm or cannot reuse the public runtime.
